A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HierarQ research. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary Sections A-E are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original HierarQ benchmark results, component ablations, robustness experiments, and qualitative analyses in the main text and supplementary material.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results across video understanding, question answering, and captioning, including the supplementary experiments and case studies.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same feature modulators, hierarchical Q-Formers, short- and long-term memory banks, FIFO/compression updates, and language-model decoding and training procedures.

E1.justification: The same ten benchmarks and task coverage remain. Supplementary LVU metadata classification and frozen-frame/out-of-distribution scenarios also appear unchanged in both versions.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across benchmark tables, ablations, and qualitative comparisons. The newly cited work in v2's introduction is background literature, not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The evaluation metrics, stated 100-frame input setting, model configurations, training settings, and Table 16 data splits are unchanged. Supplementary robustness and ablation protocols also match.

E4.justification: Sections 4.4-5 and supplementary Sections B-C retain the same component and memory ablations, video-length and parameter controls, irrelevant-frame robustness tests, and qualitative success/failure analyses.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. The same tables and plots remain, with no added or revised run counts, seed information, uncertainty reporting, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Main and supplementary numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, both versions report 67.9 LVU average accuracy in Table 1 and 87.5 MovieChat-1k global accuracy in Table 3.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(9), feature and memory definitions, attention formulations, and the memory-compression rule are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same architectural contributions, claims about handling long videos and context limits, and state-of-the-art or competitive performance claims across ten benchmarks.

C2.justification: Interpretations of complementary entity/scene processing and memory behavior are unchanged. The supplementary material retains the same spatially ambiguous counting failures and future directions involving adaptive memory and chunked processing.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 and supplementary Section D retain identical implementation, hardware, architecture, and hyperparameter information. Tables 14-16, the Figure 16 evaluation prompt, and the project-page link are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Azad et al., Understanding depth and height perception in large visual-language models (2025), as reference [5] in the introductory MLLM discussion. All 93 existing references and the substantive research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 7, Acknowledgement, crediting the Microsoft Accelerating Foundation Models Research grant program. Apart from citation renumbering and version metadata, the existing scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgement and added reference reflow the bibliography on PDF pages 9-12, with minor introductory text wrapping changes. Figures and tables retain their content, design, and placement.

improvement.justification: The funding acknowledgement and additional background citation make attribution more complete. However, the scientific exposition, methods, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, leaving no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
